gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own runtime math for the Elite 30 mini (7.7 h at 20 W) works out to 154 Wh delivered, 53% of its 288 Wh rating, where the 85% rule the rival pages use would promise 12.2 h; none works out Wh per lb (39.5 vs 31.4 for the RIVER 3) or lifetime kWh either.
standout_why: Compared against both cited pages (powersized.com Black Friday tracker, theinertia.com) and four top results (wattandwarden.com, radarofproducts.com, machinefanatic.com, thepowerstationguide.com). PowerSized gives only price, Wh, W and lb for the Elite 30 mini, with no derived figure. The Inertia lists RIVER 3 inputs (245 Wh, 7.8 lb, $200) but no usable-Wh or runtime figure. MachineFanatic and Watt & Warden apply a flat 0.85 factor with no standby term, and only to 128-192 Wh units. The Power Station Guide quotes usable-capacity ranges but nothing for the Elite 30 mini. None computes Wh per lb, $ per Wh or lifetime kWh for the under-$200 AC units. It scores 2, not 3, because I could not read a RIVER 3 price today, so cost per usable Wh against ChatGPT's other pick stays open.
decides: Confirms the BLUETTI Elite 30 mini as the pick on the derived figures I could source: 26% more Wh per lb than the RIVER 3, 2.35 times the rated lifetime energy, and $0.656-0.691 per rated Wh against $0.778 for the EcoFlow RIVER 2 240 on Amazon. It also corrects ChatGPT's runtime line for small loads: at a 20 W router or Starlink Mini load, plan on BLUETTI's own 7.7 h, not the 11-12 h the 80-85% rule implies. Two cautions: the mini is under $200 only at the Black Friday price (PowerSized's 30-day median is $239.99), and the RIVER 3 has a named-reviewer usable figure (StorageReview, 210 Wh) while the mini has none.

findings.label: Delivered energy at a 20 W load, from BLUETTI's own runtime figure
findings.value: 154 Wh, 53% of rated (7.7 h at 20 W)
findings.source_title: The Gadgeteer, Vincent Nguyen: BLUETTI Elite 30 mini launch article (published 2026-11-10, updated 2026-11-19)
findings.note: The Gadgeteer reports BLUETTI's math: Starlink Mini at 20 W for 7.7 h. 20 W x 7.7 h = 154 Wh; 154 / 288 = 53%. The flat 85% rule gives 288 x 0.85 / 20 = 12.2 h. This is a launch article with no measurements, and the output used (AC or DC) is not given.

findings.label: Standby drain on a full battery
findings.value: about 58 hours to empty at 5 W standby
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 mini Portable Power Station | 300W, 288Wh
findings.note: 288 Wh / 5 W = 57.6 h. BLUETTI says 'just 5W of standby power draw' and does not say whether that is with AC on or DC only.

findings.label: Ceiling on hours at a steady 50 W
findings.value: 5.2 h at most, before conversion loss
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 mini Portable Power Station | 300W, 288Wh
findings.note: 288 Wh / (50 W load + 5 W standby) = 5.2 h. This is an upper bound from maker figures, not a measured runtime.

findings.label: Average charge rate to 80%

findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 mini Portable Power Station | 300W, 288Wh
findings.note: 0.8 x 288 = 230.4 Wh; 230.4 / (46/60 h) = 300 W. BLUETTI's page gives the times without naming the source; The Gadgeteer says they are on AC.
